CROSS-ALBUM SLOT DECLARATIONS -- the allowlist tools/check_album_provenance.py gates.

An album slot normally holds a file encoded from that album's OWN source folder. A
slot that holds a file from a different album's folder is a decision about a
RECORDING -- the same performance shipped twice under different release names -- and
it must be written down here, with its evidence, or the gate fails.

WHY A SEPARATE FILE. build_map.py rewrites soundtracks/track_map.json from scratch,
so a declaration stored there can be erased by a regeneration; albums_manifest.json
is regenerated by gen_albums.py the same way. A declaration that a build step can
silently delete is not a declaration, so this file is owned by no generator.

WHY A DECLARATION AND NOT A HASH. track_map.json already pins every .dsp sha256 to
the source FLAC it was encoded from, and the encoder is byte-deterministic on a
pinned toolchain, so the BYTES are already proven. What nothing proved was whether
the file in a given slot is the recording that album is supposed to have: pointing
a slot at any other valid track passed every existing check.

THE RULE, exactly: for each album, the gate derives that album's own source folder
from track_map.json by name (see check_album_provenance.py's docstring), and every
slot whose file traces elsewhere must appear here with the matching album, slot and
file. The set must be EXACTLY the live bindings -- a stale, wrong, non-cross-album
or duplicated declaration fails too, so this list cannot rot. `slot` is the index
into that album's albums_manifest.json listing and is part of the identity: album
order is gameplay (music_core.cpp applyAlbumLevel maps a level to that index), so a
moved slot is a different decision and must be re-declared deliberately.

To see the live set after a deliberate change: python3 tools/check_album_provenance.py
prints the derived album->folder table and names every undeclared slot.

recording: it is the TxK recording; the retired Space Giraffe copy was the same performance looped (lag-searched cross-correlation ncc 0.9495 at lag ~0 and 0.9494 at lag ~293.28 s, self-ncc 0.9955 with a seam click at 293.257 s); the long version's extra 10.06 s closing reprise is knowingly dropped; source FLAC retained at soundtracks/Space_Giraffe/01.flac so the decision is reversible; slot index preserved to keep the level bands identical.
